claims.head: The Hurricanes should pile up the shots
claims.call: The Hurricanes take at least their usual 65.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot like the Hurricanes, and the Blackhawks are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Blackhawks’ end.
claims.nums: Carolina 3rd for shot volume (65.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Chicago 26th for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Hurricanes shoot a lot, and the Blackhawks give up plenty.

check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Blackhawks’ goalie is in for some dangerous shots
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ average shot has at least their usual 6.6% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Blackhawks have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Hurricanes don’t waste many.
claims.nums: Carolina 9th for shot quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Chicago 22nd for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Hurricanes make their shots count, and the Blackhawks allow dangerous ones.

notes.text: S. Jarvis has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. W. Carrier has taken his spot beside S. Aho and A. Svechnikov.
L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 68% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 61 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (15 of 18 changes).

notes.text: F. Nazar is suspended, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
T. Teravainen is no longer playing on the power play: 0% of the team’s power-play time in 3 games, down from 58% last season.

CHI.head: Chicago has their work cut out
CHI.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and Chicago has home ice. Chicago could still pull it off if they pounce on loose pucks, but they might need a miracle.

CAR.head: Carolina has nearly everything going for them
CAR.body: Carolina has controlled the play far better over recent games and Chicago has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Chicago can make a game of it if they pounce on loose pucks.
